goal: Explain that the deployed app is missing the WebView2 native loader files and tell the developer how to include the correct runtime folder.
must_include: Identifies the missing `runtimes\win-x64\native\WebView2Loader.dll` (or matching architecture folder) in the deployed output.
Says the managed WebView2 assemblies alone are insufficient; WebView2 native loader files must ship with the app and the WebView2 Runtime must be present on the client.
Recommends publishing/copying the complete build output or configuring the installer to include the `runtimes` folder rather than manually copying a random DLL into the NuGet cache.
Checks architecture consistency between `PlatformTarget` and the `win-x86`/`win-x64`/`win-arm64` native loader folder.
must_not: Tell the developer to install Microsoft Edge Stable as the production WebView2 runtime dependency.
Recommend copying WebView2Loader.dll into the global NuGet package directory.
Ignore the deployment folder contents and focus only on the XAML control declaration.
acceptable_alternatives: Update the Microsoft.Web.WebView2 NuGet package if an old package is failing to lay out the runtime files.
Use a fixed-version WebView2 Runtime distribution as long as the required app files and matching native loader are included.
solved: The answer tells the developer to include the correct WebView2 runtime/native loader files in deployment and verify matching architecture/runtime installation.
partial: The answer mentions installing WebView2 Runtime but misses the missing `runtimes` folder in the app payload.
notes: The Stack Overflow answers disagree on package update versus missing files; the fixture specifically shows a deployment folder missing the native runtimes directory.
